post.description:
- Open to everyone.
- Registers new user with validation and uniqueness checks.
- Passwords are peppered, salted, and stored as hashes.
- Logged-in user cannot sign up until session expires or is terminated.

- Open to everyone.
- Authenticates registered user, sets JWT with session ID in cookies, and creates session.
- Logged-in user cannot log in again until session expires or is terminated.
- Authentication renews automatically when accessing protected routes before expiration.
- If JWT is invalid, expired, or session is terminated, user loses authentication.

by_email.summary: Log in with an email address

put.description:
- Open to authenticated users.
- Current user can change their password.
- New password must differ from current password.
- Automatically revokes all existing sessions to secure the account.

delete.description:
- Open to authenticated users.
- Logs user out by deleting JWT from cookies and removing session from database.

get.description:
- Open to any authenticated caller, via whichever IdentityProvider the
  container has -- cookie session (CoreProvider) or API key
  (PublicApiProvider).
- Self-service: returns the caller's OWN profile only.
- No authorize() call -- viewing your own profile needs nothing beyond
  being an authenticated, active user.
- Bound unmodified into BOTH CoreProvider and PublicApiProvider -- the
  concrete proof that CurrentUserService abstracts over the identity
  mechanism: same class, same logic, two transports.

patch.description:
- Open to any logged-in user; edits only the caller, never an id from the path.
- A partial update: a field left out stays as it is; null clears the description.
- Every value is validated before anything changes.
- Changing the email needs the current password, like ChangePassword.
- A username, email or phone number another account has is a 409.

post.description:
- Open to admins.
- Creates new user, including admins, if the username is unique.
- Only super admins can create new admins.

get.description:
- Open to admins.
- Retrieves paginated list of existing users with relevant info.

put.description:
- Open to admins.
- Admins can set passwords of subordinate users.

- Open to super admins.
- Grants admin rights to specified user.
- Super admin rights cannot be changed.

delete.description:
- Open to super admins.
- Revokes admin rights from specified user.
- Super admin rights cannot be changed

put.description:
- Open to admins.
- Restores previously soft-deleted user.
- Only super admins can activate other admins.

delete.description:
- Open to admins.
- Soft-deletes existing user, making that user inactive.
- Also deletes user's sessions.
- Only super admins can deactivate other admins.
- Super admins cannot be soft-deleted.

patch.description:
- Open to admins; edits another user's profile.
- Admins can edit subordinate users only, as SetUserPassword.
- No password needed: the role hierarchy is the authorization.
- A partial update: a field left out stays as it is; null clears the description.
- Every value is validated before anything changes.

post.description:
- Open to any authenticated caller.
- Creates an organization, and makes the caller its OWNER -- an
  already-accepted membership, so the creator needs no self-invite.
- Both rows are staged before a single commit: one transaction, so an
  organization can never exist without its first owner.

get.description:
- Open to any authenticated caller.
- Lists the organizations the caller has an ACCEPTED membership in, with
  their own role and each organization's member count.
- User-scoped, like ListApiKeys: scoped to the caller's id by
  construction, so no organization-scoped role check is needed.

post.description:
- Only an OWNER or ADMIN of the organization may invite; a MEMBER gets
  403, a non-member 404 (via CurrentOrganizationService).
- Only an OWNER may invite someone AS an OWNER.
- The invitee must be an existing, active account, found by username.
- Creates a pending membership (accepted_at=None) that expires after
  invitation_ttl_days (ORGANIZATION_INVITATION_TTL_DAYS in production).
- An invitee who already has a live row (a membership, or a pending
  invitation that hasn't expired) is a conflict. One whose only row is
  an EXPIRED invitation gets that same row renewed instead.
- Both a new and a renewed invitation email the invitee, through an
  OrganizationInvitationCreatedEvent (SendOrganizationInvitationEmail).

invite_member.summary: Invite a user as a member

get.description:
- Open to ANY member of the organization (the lowest role), not just
  an OWNER or ADMIN; a non-member gets 404 (via CurrentOrganizationService).
- Lists every membership row, accepted and pending, with each member's
  username only -- never email or phone -- plus the member count.

post.description:
- Only the invitee may accept their own invitation. Authorization is
  "is this invitation mine?" (the CanManageSelf shape), NOT
  CurrentOrganizationService -- the invitee isn't a member yet, so
  there's no role for MembershipChecker to find.
- Someone else's invitation, an unknown id, or one from another
  organization all look the same: MembershipNotFoundError (404).
- Idempotent: accepting an already-accepted membership changes nothing
  and commits nothing, so a retried request is safe (like RevokeApiKey).
- An expired invitation can't be accepted: InvitationExpiredError (410).

- Only the invitee may decline their own invitation -- the same
  "is this invitation mine?" rule as AcceptOrganizationInvitation.
- Declining DELETES the pending row, whether or not it has expired
  (clearing away a lapsed invitation is harmless). No clock is needed.
- Only PENDING invitations can be declined. An accepted membership is
  reported as not found: leaving goes through RemoveOrganizationMember,
  which enforces that the last OWNER can never leave.
- Missing, not yours, another organization's, or already accepted: all
  the same MembershipNotFoundError (404).

delete.description:
- Deletes a membership row, pending or accepted.
- Removing YOURSELF is leaving: any member may leave.
- Removing someone else needs ADMIN. Removing a pending row is how an
  admin revokes an invitation.
- Only an OWNER may remove another OWNER (pending OWNER invites included).
- The last ACCEPTED owner can never be removed, including by leaving.

patch.description:
- Needs ADMIN (403 for a MEMBER, 404 for a non-member).
- Only an OWNER may change an OWNER's role, or grant the OWNER role.
- Demoting the last ACCEPTED owner is refused. Promoting someone else
  to OWNER first is how ownership is transferred.
- Works on a pending invitation's role too, under the same rules.

get.description:
- Open to any authenticated caller.
- Lists the caller's own PENDING, unexpired invitations, across every
  organization, with the ids the accept/decline routes need.
- User-scoped, NOT organization-scoped: the invitee isn't a member yet,
  so an organization role check would reject them by definition.

delete.description:
- Only an OWNER may delete the organization: an ADMIN or MEMBER gets 403,
  a non-member 404 (via CurrentOrganizationService).
- Deletes the organization row only. Every membership and invitation goes
  with it through the database's ON DELETE CASCADE.
- Irreversible: there is no soft delete.

patch.description:
- Needs ADMIN (403 for a MEMBER, 404 for a non-member).
- A partial update: a field left out stays as it is. Neither the name nor
  the description can be cleared.
- Both values are validated before either changes, so an invalid
  description never leaves a half-applied rename behind.

both_fields.summary: Change the name and the description

What an account can do INSIDE one specific organization. Deliberately
independent of UserRole (types_.py), which governs what an account can
do to the platform itself -- the two role lists never reference each
other.

UpdateOwnProfileRequestSchema.title: UpdateOwnProfileRequestSchema
UpdateOwnProfileRequestSchema.description:
Using Pydantic model here is generally unnecessary.
It's only implemented to render specific Swagger UI.

A field left out is MISSING (pydantic's "not sent" sentinel), turned into
core's OMITTED before the handler sees it, so a PATCH changes only what's
sent; the description alone can also be null, which clears it
(docs/plans/10-profile-editing.md, decision 3).
